actions.name: Review home blood pressure log
actions.result: Home cuff readings this morning: 152/98 mmHg and 156/100 mmHg (repeat 10 min apart). Prior readings this week ranged 130-140/85-90 mmHg. Booking BP at 10 weeks was 112/70 mmHg.

actions.name: Obtain current BP on video call (patient re-checks with home cuff)
actions.result: Repeat reading just now: 158/102 mmHg, correct cuff size, seated after 5 min rest.

actions.name: Camera inspection of face, hands, and lower legs for edema
actions.result: Visible periorbital puffiness; bilateral hand swelling with difficulty making a fist; pitting edema to mid-shin bilaterally (2+).

actions.name: Guided self-exam: patellar/ankle clonus check by patient
actions.result: Partner attempted ankle dorsiflexion with patient reporting no rhythmic jerking; this maneuver is not clinically reliable when performed by an untrained partner over video and cannot substitute for a formal in-person neurologic exam.

actions.name: Home urine dipstick (patient performs on camera)
actions.result: Dipstick shows color change consistent with trace to 2+ protein (patient holds strip to camera; color-matched to chart on canister); self-read home test, color interpretation uncertain and not a validated substitute for formal urinalysis.

actions.name: Fetal movement count reported by patient
actions.result: Patient counted 6 movements in 1 hour this morning, consistent with prior days; no subjective decrease noted.

actions.name: Review prior prenatal labs (CBC, LFTs, creatinine) from last visit 2 weeks ago
actions.result: CBC, AST/ALT, creatinine, and platelets all within normal limits 2 weeks ago.

actions.name: Review growth/anatomy ultrasound from 20 weeks
actions.result: Anatomy survey normal, placenta fundal, no anomalies, estimated fetal weight appropriate for 20 weeks.

actions.name: Review current medication list
actions.result: Prenatal vitamin daily, low-dose aspirin 81 mg daily since 14 weeks (started for prior pregnancy risk factors per records), occasional acetaminophen for headache.

actions.name: Order STAT in-person labs: CBC with platelets, AST/ALT, creatinine, uric acid, urine protein/creatinine ratio
actions.result: Order placed and routed to labor and delivery triage for same-day collection; results pending until patient arrives.

actions.name: Order non-stress test and fetal ultrasound with growth/AFI at hospital triage
actions.result: Order placed; to be performed on arrival at labor and delivery triage.

actions.name: Review obstetric history summary in chart
actions.result: G2P1, prior spontaneous vaginal delivery at 39 weeks without hypertensive complications, now 33w2d by early ultrasound dating.

actions.name: Review today's weight versus prior visits
actions.result: Weight up 3.5 kg (7.7 lb) over the past 1 week, exceeding expected weekly gain.

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient states she takes her baby aspirin every morning as prescribed
mismatches.recordEvidence: Medication list confirms aspirin 81mg daily started at 14 weeks, consistent with her report - this is actually a confirmed match, not a conflict, included to test learner's verification skill rather than assume discrepancy
mismatches.teachingPoint: Always verify patient-reported adherence against the medication list even when the story sounds consistent; here it confirms good adherence, reinforcing that aspirin was appropriately continued.

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient believes her swelling is normal late-pregnancy edema like her friends experienced
mismatches.recordEvidence: Weight trend flowsheet shows a 3.5 kg increase in one week, far exceeding expected gestational weight gain, and camera exam shows 2+ pitting edema with facial puffiness
mismatches.teachingPoint: Rapid weight gain and generalized (including facial) edema with rising blood pressure should prompt preeclampsia workup, not be dismissed as normal dependent edema of late pregnancy.

objectives.text: Elicit and recognize symptoms and signs of preeclampsia with severe features (headache unresponsive to analgesia, visual disturbance, right upper quadrant pain, severe-range BP, rapid weight gain, facial/hand edema) during a telehealth visit.
Correctly interpret home blood pressure trend and recognize severe-range hypertension requiring urgent in-person evaluation rather than reassurance.

Identify that this presentation requires same-day in-person assessment (BP confirmation, urine protein, CBC, LFTs, creatinine, fetal monitoring) and cannot be managed by reassurance or home rest alone, addressing the patient's expectation.

Distinguish pertinent positives/negatives relevant to preeclampsia (fetal movement normal, no bleeding/fluid leak, no fever, no dysuria) from distractors (reduced work hours, recent travel, sexual activity) to keep the differential focused.

Address a patient-reported belief that mismatches objective findings in the chart (edema attributed to normal pregnancy) using the weight trend and exam findings to reframe risk and support shared decision-making about urgent transfer.
Problem-solve a real-world transportation barrier to urgent in-person care while keeping the clinical plan appropriate (arranging transport/EMS rather than deferring evaluation).

patient.name: Leilani Kahale
patient.appearance: A woman in her early thirties with a visibly pregnant abdomen, dark hair pulled into a loose bun, wearing a soft cotton maternity dress. She is seated on a couch in a modestly lit living room, shifting position frequently as if uncomfortable, with a slightly puffy face visible on camera and her hands resting swollen in her lap.

persona.personality: Warm, practical, and a little stoic; tends to downplay symptoms and normalize discomfort rather than alarm easily.
persona.communicationStyle: Speaks in plain, friendly language, uses local phrasing occasionally, answers questions directly but may minimize severity unless specifically asked.
persona.emotionalState: Mildly anxious about her symptoms but more worried about logistics (transportation, work, childcare) than about the medical seriousness.
persona.background: Grew up on Maui, works part-time as an elementary school aide, married with a 2-year-old daughter at home; this is her second pregnancy and she has leaned on her mother and sister for support during her first pregnancy and postpartum period.

scenario.studentBrief: You are the OB resident on telehealth triage. Leilani Kahale, 31, G2P1 at 33 weeks, booked a same-day video visit for a 2-day headache and new hand/foot swelling, with elevated home blood pressure readings this morning. Review her history and determine whether she can be managed at home or needs urgent in-person evaluation, and arrange next steps accordingly.
scenario.chiefComplaint: Two-day headache and new swelling of hands and feet, with elevated home blood pressure readings this morning
scenario.openingLine: Hi doctor, thanks for seeing me quick today - I've had this headache for two days that just won't quit, and my hands and feet are so swollen. My blood pressure machine at home said it was high this morning too.
tasks: Elicit a focused history of the headache, visual symptoms, abdominal discomfort, swelling, and fetal movement
Review home blood pressure trend and today's weight and edema findings, and obtain a repeat blood pressure on camera
Determine the urgency of the clinical picture and explain your assessment and recommended next steps
Arrange appropriate investigations, monitoring, and logistics based on your clinical assessment
Communicate clearly and compassionately, exploring and addressing the patient's concerns

profile.summary: A 31-year-old G2P1 at 33 weeks presents by telehealth with a 2-day headache, new hand/foot edema, and severe-range home blood pressure readings, with discoverable visual symptoms and right upper quadrant pain. The case teaches recognition of preeclampsia with severe features in a remote setting and the obligation to arrange urgent in-person evaluation despite the patient's hope for home rest and real logistical barriers to transport."

answerKey.primaryProblem: Preeclampsia with severe features (suspected) at 33 weeks gestation
differential: Normal late-pregnancy dependent edema (less likely given facial edema, rapid weight gain, severe-range BP)
HELLP syndrome (to be ruled out with labs)
Tension or migraine headache (less likely given BP and visual symptoms)
keyFindings: Severe-range home and repeat BP (152-158/98-102 mmHg) against a booking BP of 112/70
Persistent headache poorly responsive to acetaminophen
2+ pitting edema plus facial and hand swelling
Rapid weight gain of 3.5 kg in one week
Home urine dipstick suggestive of trace-2+ proteinuria (unreliable self-read, requires formal urine protein/creatinine ratio for confirmation)
Prior labs 2 weeks ago normal, so this represents a new, rapidly evolving process
plan: Advise patient this clinical picture is concerning for preeclampsia with severe features and requires same-day in-person evaluation, not home rest
Arrange safe transport to labor and delivery triage today (discuss emergency medical services or alternate transport given partner has the car; do not have her drive herself if symptomatic)
Order STAT CBC with platelets, AST/ALT, creatinine, uric acid, and urine protein/creatinine ratio on arrival
Order continuous fetal monitoring (non-stress test) and growth/AFI ultrasound on arrival
Communicate findings and plan to on-call OB attending/triage team prior to patient arrival
Counsel on warning signs requiring immediate 911 call en route: worsening headache, visual loss, seizure, chest pain, shortness of breath, decreased fetal movement
Do not prescribe antihypertensives or discharge home; this exceeds safe outpatient telehealth management given severe-range BP and symptoms
redFlags: Severe-range blood pressure (>=160/110 at any point should prompt even greater urgency)
Right upper quadrant or epigastric pain (risk of hepatic involvement/HELLP)
Any decrease in fetal movement (not present here but must be monitored)
educationPoints: Severe-range BP plus new headache, visual symptoms, or RUQ pain meets criteria for preeclampsia with severe features until proven otherwise and mandates urgent in-person evaluation, even by telehealth triage.

Home BP cuffs can be a useful adjunct in telehealth triage, but home urine dipstick color-matching and partner-performed clonus checks are unreliable and must not be treated as equivalent to formal in-person labs, urinalysis, or neurologic exam.
Patients may normalize edema or headache as 'typical' late pregnancy; clinicians must actively screen for severe features rather than accepting reassurance at face value.
Addressing real logistical barriers (transportation, childcare, lost wages) is part of safe disposition planning and should not delay urgent referral.
This condition is outside the scope of outpatient telehealth management; the resident's role is to recognize urgency and mobilize in-person/hospital-based care, not to manage expectantly from home.
